## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove all items from the rear end of the truck.
2. Test fit a hitch flip to check clearance and alignment.
3. Hammer the bottom of the hitch bracket against the frame rails until it wedges flush between them.
4. Use a screwdriver to align bolt holes on the hitch with those in the frame stiffener.
5. Drop the frame stiffener into place so its flat side faces outward.
6. [Partial] Mark and cut away sections of the stock bumper where they interfere with the raised hitch.
7. Drill mounting holes through the bumper, frame, and bracket assembly to secure everything together.

_Procedure reported by [t1063]._

## Specifications

- **Angle Iron Size Options**: 3"x3" or 3.5"x3.5" [t1638] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Channel Steel Size**: C8x11.25 [t1638] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Cut Angle**: 45* [t1638] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Engine/tranny skid price (Rocky Road)**: $356 [t1411] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Front skid price (Rocky Road)**: $139 [t1411] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Hinge Tube Outer Diameter**: 2.25" [t1638] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Material thickness**: 3/16" [t1488] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Plate material thickness**: 3/16" [t1411] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Primary bend angle**: 90° [t1487] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Secondary bend angle (suspected)**: 60° [t1487] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Sheet dimensions**: 4x8 [t1488] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Sheet metal thickness**: 3/16" [t1487] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Sheet metal weight per foot**: 11.5 lbs. [t1487] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Square Tubing Dimensions**: 2"x2" [t1638] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Stock mounting bolt count per side**: 3 bolts on each side and one up front on each side (total 8) [t1419] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Winch capacity fitment**: 8-10k pounds standard, up to 12k possible [t1419] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Utilizes the factory bumper hardware instead of buying a custom one. [t1045]
- Use masking or painter's tape over the fender area before drilling to prevent paint chipping. [t2131]
- The kit includes extra parts, but you likely won't need half of them; keep extras for future projects. [t2131]
- Use a flat-tip screwdriver to force hose clamps under plastic ends of the ducting for a tight seal. [t2131]
- Move or push the ducting deeper into the fender if needed so the panel fits back on cleanly. [t2131]
- Reattach the stock airbox to its location before final assembly for easier access later. [t2131]
- [Partial] Ensure cuts are precise so the rubber looks clean and fits snugly like it was factory installed. [t2131]
- Use a toilet paper roll as a form to trace and cut tubing contours. [t1487]
- Grind the traced tube sections until they match the desired shape. [t1487]
- Round tubing is easier to work with than square or rectangular sections. [t1487]
- [Partial] Full width C-channel provides a robust alternative to notched DOM tubing. [t1487]
- [Partial] Ensure the secondary angle measurement is taken correctly from the top piece to avoid acute angles. [t1487]
- Consider leaving the valance piece off to prevent it from breaking soon. [t1412]
- Look for a slightly raised lip on the cross shaft side where the spacer fits. [t1757]
- Use a steel step bit to drill holes slightly larger than needed. [t1063]
- Apply C-channel molding and black silicone over cut edges for a finished look. [t1063]
- Use buttoncap heads instead of hex heads to solve the exposed bolt head issue. [t1411]
- [Partial] Ensure you get super hard variety buttoncaps for better damage resistance. [t1411]
- Use the same hardware that held the original bumper if available. [t1419]
- [Partial] Consider using PB Blast to clean rusted bolts before removal. [t1419]
- Position shackle mounts on the sides or front to allow pulley use and increase pulling power. [t1419]
- Anchor clevises directly to frame horns for the strongest pull points. [t1419]
- [Partial] Paint just the bars while installed for easier access, though it is more difficult than painting before installation. [t1419]
- [Partial] Use bed liner instead of primer if concerned about plastic side panels peeling. [t1419]
- [Partial] Wire the lights to use the existing fog light switch on the blinker arm. [t1419]
- Select a round light for proper aesthetics if using single bolt tabs. [t1419]
- Consider adding a top hoop if the body is lifted and space exists above. [t1802]
- [Partial] Ensure mounts are raised 2 inches taller if lifting the body to maintain coverage over frame horns. [t1802]
- [Partial] Note that the Pre-runner style is distinct from standard full-plated designs but offers more visual appeal. [t1803]
- Custom fabrication may be required to achieve specific tube setups not found in stock options. [t1803]
- Ideal if you do not need the hitch for frequent towing. [t1416]
- Best suited as an occasional addition rather than permanent hardware. [t1416]
- Allow at least two full days for the vehicle to be available while James builds it. [t1619]
- [Partial] Consider a 'swing-away' design if you need extra storage space without permanently blocking the rear view. [t1638]
- If buying from a middleman (like AC), verify shipping times as they may not keep stock in house. [t1638]
- Look for shackle mounts that align directly with the frame to reduce stress points. [t1638]
- Use this channel steel to replace plastic bumpettes and create a squared-off look. [t1638]
- [Partial] Add side pieces of C8 cut at 45 degrees on one end for tire carrier support. [t1638]
- [Partial] Mount the spindle on the face of the bumper rather than the top to prevent leverage issues when rear-ended. [t1638]
- [Partial] Face mounting braces the swing arm better against impacts and keeps the center of gravity lower. [t1638]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Using an incorrect 60-degree angle which results in a more acute shape than intended. [t1487]
- [Partial] Mounting cross pieces for tire carriers with limited room for error due to tight angles. [t1487]
- [Partial] Using a sheet that is too small for the rocky terrain. [t1488]
- [Partial] Using standard hex bolts which can tear out or wallow holes in the frame over time. [t1411]
- [Partial] Waiting too long for factory-style bumpers and missing off-road opportunities due to delivery delays. [t1638]
- [Partial] Buying a bumper with an offset tire carrier mount without considering how it affects departure angles in deep sand or rock crawling. [t1638]
